docs.title: Productive K3s Adapters
docs.text:
Build-time conversion from external application formats to native Productive K3s artifacts.

Compose first. Extensible by design. Runtime-independent by rule.

docs.title: Productive K3s Adapters
docs.text: Adapters converts external application definitions into reviewable, self-contained Productive K3s artifacts.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Use Python 3.10+. Run make install-dev, make test, make lint, and make smoke-adaptation.

docs.title: Adding adapters
docs.text: An adapter parses one source ecosystem into the internal Application/Service model. It must not contain deployment logic.

docs.title: Adding resolvers
docs.text: Implement Resolver.matches() and Resolver.resolve(), then register the resolver before the generic fallback in resolvers/registry.py.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Source specification → Adapter → Normalized model → Resolver → Target → PK3S Stack

The conversion is build-time. Deployment never depends on Adapters.

docs.title: Docker Compose adapter
docs.text: The first adapter reads an already-built Compose definition. Services using build: without an image: are rejected intentionally: image building belongs to OpenShip or another upstream producer.

docs.title: Output contract
docs.text: A conversion emits stack.yaml, one values file per component, a human-readable README and conversion-report.json with warnings/TODOs. The current Stack schema is marked v1alpha1 until aligned with the canonical Productive K3s Stack contract.

docs.title: Resolver model
docs.text: Resolvers classify normalized services. PostgreSQL, Redis and MinIO currently receive dedicated community chart references. Unknown application containers fall back to Stakater Application.

docs.title: OpenShip workflow
docs.text:
OpenShip remains independent. Its responsibility ends when it produces Docker/Compose artifacts. Adapters begins at that artifact boundary.

Git repo → OpenShip → Compose → Adapters → PK3S Stack → catalog

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
pk3s-adapters validate compose compose.yaml
pk3s-adapters inspect compose compose.yaml
pk3s-adapters convert compose compose.yaml --name my-app --output ./my-app-stack

docs.title: Productive K3s Adapters
docs.text: Adapters convierte definiciones externas de aplicaciones en artefactos Productive K3s autocontenidos y revisables.

docs.title: Desarrollo
docs.text: Usar Python 3.10+. Ejecutar make install-dev, make test, make lint y make smoke-adaptation.

docs.title: Agregar adapters
docs.text: Un adapter convierte un formato fuente al modelo interno Application/Service. No debe desplegar al cluster.

docs.title: Agregar resolvers
docs.text: Implementar Resolver.matches() y Resolver.resolve(), y registrarlo antes del fallback generico en resolvers/registry.py.

docs.title: Arquitectura
docs.text:
Especificacion origen → Adapter → Modelo normalizado → Resolver → Target → PK3S Stack

La conversion ocurre en build-time. El despliegue nunca depende de Adapters.

docs.title: Adapter Docker Compose
docs.text: El primer adapter lee una definicion Compose ya construida. Si un servicio usa build: sin image:, se rechaza: construir imagenes corresponde a OpenShip u otra herramienta anterior en el pipeline.

docs.title: Contrato de salida
docs.text: La conversion genera stack.yaml, values por componente, README y conversion-report.json. El esquema Stack actual se marca v1alpha1 hasta alinearlo exactamente con el contrato canonico de Productive K3s.

docs.title: Modelo de resolvers
docs.text: Los resolvers clasifican servicios normalizados. PostgreSQL, Redis y MinIO reciben referencias a charts comunitarios. Los contenedores genericos usan Stakater Application como fallback.

docs.title: Flujo con OpenShip
docs.text: OpenShip permanece independiente. Su responsabilidad termina al producir Docker/Compose. Adapters comienza exactamente en ese limite.

docs.title: Uso
docs.text:
pk3s-adapters validate compose compose.yaml
pk3s-adapters inspect compose compose.yaml
pk3s-adapters convert compose compose.yaml --name my-app --output ./my-app-stack
